en: The Welwitschia plant in the Namib Desert survives for over a thousand years with only two continuously growing leaves.
Wombats produce cube-shaped feces to stop their droppings from rolling away when marking their territory on rocks and logs.
The cells lining your stomach completely replace themselves every three to four days to prevent the acid from digesting it.
The adult stage of a mayfly lasts only twenty-four hours, making it the shortest-lived insect in the world.
Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor but support twenty-five percent of all marine species.
The wood frog survives harsh winters by freezing almost completely solid and temporarily stopping its heart and breathing.
Your small intestine is about twenty feet long and absorbs most of the nutrients from the food you eat.
The archerfish shoots precise jets of water from its mouth to knock insects off overhanging branches into the water.
Some species of bamboo can grow up to thirty-five inches in a single day, making it the fastest-growing plant.
Babies are born with about three hundred bones, but adults only have two hundred six because many fuse together.
Pacific salmon swim hundreds of miles upstream from the ocean to the exact freshwater stream where they hatched to spawn.
A blue whale's heart is the size of a small car and beats only eight to ten times per minute.
